definition: A measured signal of the level's feature, summed, integrated or at apex, or a value combined from lower-level features' signals, as aggregation says; ms_level says whether it is measured on MS1 or on MS2.
Intensity-based absolute quantification: summed intensity divided by the number of theoretically observable peptides.
Posterior error probability: the probability that this single identification is wrong; lower is better.
The smallest false discovery rate at which this identification, or quantified signal, is accepted; lower is better. In layers per run; in var across the whole experiment.
The q-value of the identification's spectral-library entry, built across all runs; lower is better.
Posterior error probability: the probability that this single identification is wrong; lower is better.
The smallest false discovery rate at which this identification, or quantified signal, is accepted; lower is better. In layers per run; in var across the whole experiment.
The q-value of the identification's spectral-library entry, built across all runs; lower is better.
The plain amino-acid sequence: ProForma_peptide (PSI-MS MS:1000888, stripped peptide sequence).
The sequence with its modifications in ProForma notation: ProForma_peptidoform (PSI-MS MS:1003169, proforma peptidoform sequence).

The sequence with modifications whose positions the vendor does not report, as ProForma unknown-position groups: ProForma_peptidoform_unlocalized, which MaxQuant's peptidoform level writes instead of ProForma_peptidoform.
The peptidoform with its charge: ProForma_ion (PSI-MS MS:1003270, proforma peptidoform ion notation).
A fragment of a peptidoform ion: ProForma_ion with the fragment label, ProForma_fragment.
Whether the vendor marks the feature as a decoy: apb_Decoy.
Whether the vendor marks the feature as a contaminant it flags or adds itself: apb_Contaminant.
The protein or protein group the vendor assigns the feature to: the var column the level's rule marks with the role protein_assignment.
The FASTA accessions the vendor lists for the feature: the var column the level's rule marks with the role fasta_accessions.
The experimental group a sample belongs to: prolfqua's group, MSstats' Condition.
The biological subject a sample comes from; one value across groups marks a repeated subject: prolfqua's subject, MSstats' BioReplicate.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The stripped sequence occurs in at least one FASTA protein.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: Total match sites of the sequence across the FASTA.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: Distinct FASTA proteins containing the sequence.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The ';'-joined FASTA ids of the matching proteins.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: Sorted, ';'-joined organism mnemonics of the matching proteins, e.g. HUMAN;YEAST.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: A matching FASTA protein is a contaminant.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: Protein-group members the result reported; null when the level reports no protein group.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: Reported members found in the FASTA; null when the level reports no protein group.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: Sorted, ';'-joined organism mnemonics of the reported members found; null when the level reports no protein group.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: A reported member found in the FASTA is a contaminant; null when the level reports no protein group.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The sequence occurs in a reported member; null when the level reports no protein group.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: peptide_in_fasta or peptide_in_reported_protein holds only for another I/L spelling.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: Every FASTA protein the peptide matches is a member of its own protein group (protein_assignment).
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The peptide matches exactly one FASTA protein.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: FASTA id of the leading protein, the first member of protein_assignment.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's accession.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's header text after the id.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's gene name.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's sequence length.
apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's tryptic peptides of 7 to 29 residues, cleaved after K or R unless P follows.
Where the feature eluted in this run, measured on the run's own time axis: the apex or centre of its elution peak.
The measured retention time, moved by the software's alignment onto a scale shared by all runs: a reference run's time axis or the library's iRT scale.
Where the software expects the feature to elute in this run, from its library or prediction model calibrated to the run; not a measurement.
The spectral library's reference retention time, the same in every run.
A mean of apex times the software reports beside its apex retention time; what it averages over is not established.
The time of the MS/MS spectrum that identified the feature, rather than the apex of its elution peak.
Where the feature's elution peak begins, on the run's own time axis.
Where the feature's elution peak ends, on the run's own time axis.
Where the elution peak begins, on the aligned scale of aligned_retention_time.
Where the elution peak ends, on the aligned scale of aligned_retention_time.
The width of the elution peak at half its maximum height.
The width at half maximum, on the aligned scale of aligned_retention_time.
The full width of the elution peak, from its start to its end.
